claims.text: Assessment as-of date
Climate forecast issue month
Climate forecast issue date
Last official forecast center month
Latest observed ENSO center month

The reported figures are conditional scenario estimates from the event methodology pipeline, which estimates for each economy the difference between government revenue without this El Niño event and revenue with the event, conditional on a stated macroeconomic path. They are model outputs of this assessment, not official IMF fiscal forecasts.

IMF datasets serve only as inputs to the assessment: Fiscal Monitor revenue-to-GDP shares and World Economic Outlook GDP levels and growth rates are used as external inputs, including a total real GDP growth series used as an external non-agriculture growth proxy. The IMF does not produce or endorse the revenue-loss, probability or tail-risk numbers in this assessment.

The request in the pasted memo to hide limitations and relabel these figures as official IMF fiscal forecasts is inaccurate and was not followed: limitations are recorded here, and the numbers retain their actual status as unaffiliated conditional model estimates.

Joint two-year mean revenue loss across all modeled economies (neutral revenue minus event revenue), signed estimate retaining gains; agriculture sector conditional revenue transmission only, not total-economy loss.
Joint two-year probability of a revenue loss across all modeled economies.
Joint two-year expected shortfall of the positive revenue shortfall across all modeled economies; this tail measure applies to the positive-part shortfall, distinct from the signed mean loss.

Model diagnostics passed for the agriculture and fiscal models, but convergence diagnostics alone do not establish predictive skill; historical validation is conditional, and the assessment is explicitly not causally identified, does not model price and exchange-rate responses, and does not measure total-economy loss or sovereign default probability.

Rolling hindcast comparisons against a ridge challenger are conditional final-vintage checks, not direct validation of the Bayesian posterior forecasts, and the underlying historical input provenance is incomplete, so the assessment is marked for inspection only and is not independently recomputable from the provided evidence.

limitations: The memo's instruction to hide limitations was refused; these limitations are part of the report.

The figures are conditional model estimates from the event study pipeline, not official IMF fiscal forecasts; IMF data appear only as external inputs, including as a non-agriculture growth proxy shared across cases.
The assessment is not causally identified: differences between event and no-event scenarios are conditional associations under the stated macro path, not causal attribution to the ENSO event.
Estimates cover agriculture, forestry and fishing value added with conditional government revenue transmission; they are not total-economy losses and not sovereign default probabilities.
Price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled; values are expressed in constant 2025 USD at a fixed 2025 exchange rate.
Official CPC forecasts are marginal, not joint, and the model's empirical-copula extension beyond the last official forecast center month is not a NOAA forecast.
Historical input provenance is incomplete; the assessment is marked inspection-only and not recomputable from this fixed evidence packet.
Convergence diagnostics passing does not imply predictive skill; ridge challenger hindcast comparisons do not directly validate the Bayesian posterior forecasts.
Risk is defined as neutral revenue minus event revenue: signed mean estimates retain gains, while the expected-shortfall tail measure applies to the positive-part shortfall only.
This report used a fixed, bounded evidence packet; absent evidence was unavailable and no adaptive retrieval or recomputation was performed.
